items.fact: subtracting the max logit leaves the softmax unchanged; LSE = m + ln sum e^(z - m)
BCEWithLogitsLoss is 'more numerically stable than using a plain Sigmoid followed by a BCELoss' because of 'the log-sum-exp trick'; CrossEntropyLoss takes 'unnormalized logits'

items.fact: Nothing takes the log of, or divides by, a saturated probability; CrossEntropyLoss takes logits; LSE trick with m = max; for logits (1000, 1001), e^1001 overflows even in float64 while the trick gives 1001 + log(e^-1 + 1) = 1001.313
items.where: Reading section 9 ('The old Topic: math child page's example ... 1001.313 the same way (rechecked)')

items.fact: Log of a softmax in two steps underflows to log 0 for tiny probabilities; use the fused log-softmax
items.status: verified (measured: naive loss inf, gradient NaN in PyTorch 2.14.1)
items.where: Reading section 9 (log-softmax), section 12 (the real hunt), section 14 (mistakes)

items.from: old child 'Information theory for ML', common mistakes
items.fact: Assigning probability exactly 0 gives infinite cross-entropy and forward KL; implementations compute log-probabilities with a log-softmax rather than the log of a softmax output that can underflow to 0
items.where: Reading section 9 (log-softmax paragraph); the KL part is owned by the Information theory page, linked in Further reading
